tracks.title: Foundations
tracks.blurb: The concepts behind the products — what local SEO, AEO/GEO, AI voice, reviews, Google profiles and content marketing actually are. Learn these first; every product sits on top of them.

modules.title: Local SEO 101 — getting found by people searching nearby

questions.q: According to Google's Business Profile help documentation, what three factors does Google use to rank local results?
options: Keywords, backlinks, and page speed
Relevance, distance, and prominence
Reviews, photos, and hours
Budget, ad spend, and bid amount
questions.explain: The lesson states Google's own documentation lists relevance, distance, and prominence as the three local ranking factors.

questions.q: Which two of Google's three local ranking factors does a business mostly control?
options: Distance and prominence
Relevance and distance
Relevance and prominence
Distance and intent
questions.explain: The lesson's rule of thumb says you mostly control relevance and prominence but cannot control distance.

questions.q: What does NAP consistency mean in local SEO?
options: Name, Address, and Phone number written identically everywhere online
Number of Active Profiles kept up to date
New Appointments Posted on the profile
Name, Account, and Password matching across sites
questions.explain: The lesson defines NAP consistency as Name, Address, and Phone number written identically everywhere online.

questions.q: Roughly what share of all Google searches does the lesson say have local intent?
options: About 12%
About 25%
About 46%
About 75%
questions.explain: The lesson states roughly 46% of all Google searches have local intent.

modules.title: AEO & GEO 101 — getting recommended by AI search

questions.q: What is the core mindset shift of AEO/GEO compared to classic SEO?
options: You buy ad placement inside AI answers
You aim to rank #1 in ChatGPT
There is no 'position' to win; the goal is to be included and cited in the AI's answer
You optimize purely for backlinks
questions.explain: The lesson stresses there is no ranked position in AI answers; the goal is to be included and recommended within the synthesized answer.

questions.q: What does RAG (retrieval-augmented generation) describe in how AI engines build answers?
options: The engine retrieves relevant web pages first, then generates an answer grounded in them
The engine ranks all websites then averages them
The engine randomly assigns generated authority
The engine generates an answer first, then retrieves links to match
questions.explain: The lesson defines RAG as retrieving relevant pages first, then generating a written answer grounded in those pages.

questions.q: Per the Princeton-led GEO paper, adding specific statistics to content boosted AI visibility by up to what amount?
options: Up to +10%
Up to +40%
Up to +115%
Up to +200%
questions.explain: The lesson reports the GEO paper found adding specific statistics boosted visibility up to +40%.

questions.q: How do teams measure AEO/GEO success since there is no rank report?
options: Total backlinks earned
Organic traffic from blue links
Page load speed across engines
AI Share of Voice — how often the business is mentioned or cited versus competitors
questions.explain: The lesson explains success is tracked via AI Share of Voice: mention/citation frequency versus competitors across representative questions.

modules.title: AI Voice 101 — how AI answers the phone

questions.q: What three stages make up the typical AI voice agent pipeline?
options: STT (hear), LLM (think), TTS (speak)
Crawl, index, rank
Listen, transfer, record
Dial, ring, voicemail
questions.explain: The lesson describes the STT to LLM to TTS pipeline as ears, brain, and mouth.

questions.q: What latency window does the lesson cite as the benchmark most production voice agents aim for?
options: 1-2 seconds
2-3 seconds
questions.explain: The lesson cites roughly 500ms as natural, with most production agents aiming for a 300-800ms window.

questions.q: What is 'grounding' in the context of an AI voice agent?
options: Limiting the agent to one phone line
Recording every call for compliance
Feeding the agent the business's real, current facts so answers come from a trusted source, not guesses
Forwarding calls to voicemail after hours
questions.explain: The lesson defines grounding as feeding the agent real business facts so answers are factual rather than guessed.

questions.q: What does 'barge-in' allow during a call with an AI voice agent?
options: The agent to transfer to a human automatically
The caller to interrupt the agent while it's talking and have it stop to listen
The agent to place the caller on hold
Two callers to join the same line
questions.explain: The lesson defines barge-in as the caller interrupting the agent while it talks, causing it to stop and listen.

modules.title: Reviews & Reputation 101 — the trust engine of local business

questions.q: What is 'review gating' as defined in the lesson?
options: Charging customers to leave a review
Deleting all reviews older than a year
Requiring login before posting a review
Routing only happy customers to public review sites while steering unhappy ones to a private form
questions.explain: The lesson defines review gating as selectively sending happy customers to public sites and unhappy ones to private feedback instead.

questions.q: Under the FTC's 2024 rule, what is the current maximum civil penalty per violation cited in the lesson?
options: Up to $53,088 per violation
Up to $5,000 per violation
Up to $1 million per violation
Up to $10,000 per violation
questions.explain: The lesson states the FTC can seek civil penalties currently up to $53,088 per violation (the 2025 level, held for 2026).

questions.q: What is the single most effective tactic the lesson recommends for ethically generating reviews?
options: Offer a discount in exchange for a 5-star review
Ask every customer right after the visit and make it one tap
Only ask customers you expect to be happy
Buy reviews from a reputable directory
questions.explain: The lesson says the most effective tactic is asking every customer right after the visit and making it one tap.

questions.q: Why can a perfect 5.0 rating with few reviews actually hurt a salon?
options: Google automatically caps ratings at 4.9
It increases the cost of advertising
A wall of nothing-but-5-stars can read as fake and thin counts seem unproven
Customers prefer salons with no reviews
questions.explain: The lesson notes a flawless rating with few reviews can read as fake, while a 4.7 with hundreds of reviews is more persuasive.

modules.title: Google Business Profile 101 — your storefront on Google

questions.q: Which Google Business Profile field is described as the single strongest controllable ranking lever?
options: The primary category
The business description
The number of photos
The website link
questions.explain: The lesson identifies the primary category as the #1 local pack ranking factor and strongest controllable lever.

questions.q: In 2025, what verification method does Google most often require for a Business Profile?
options: A mailed postcard code only
Video verification — an unedited walkthrough of the business
An email confirmation only
A notarized legal document
questions.explain: The lesson states Google most often requires video verification, an unedited walkthrough showing the storefront and interior.

questions.q: According to the lesson, fully populated, verified profiles appear about how much more often than incomplete ones?
options: About 20% more often
About 50% more often
About 80% more often
About 200% more often
questions.explain: The lesson states fully populated, verified profiles appear roughly 80% more often than incomplete ones.

questions.q: What is happening to the traditional Q&A tab on Google Business Profiles?
options: It is being expanded with video answers
It is being moved to the website only
It is being phased out and replaced by an AI-generated 'Ask about this place' answer
It now requires a paid subscription
questions.explain: The lesson says the Q&A tab is being phased out in favor of an AI-generated 'Ask about this place' answer drawn from profile data.

modules.title: SEO & Content 101 — how search ranking really works

questions.q: What are the three stages of how Google Search works, per Google's documentation?
options: Search, click, convert
Crawl, index, rank
Relevance, distance, prominence
On-page, technical, off-page
questions.explain: The lesson states Google works in three stages: crawl (discover), index (understand and store), and rank (order results).

questions.q: What does the 'extra E' in E-E-A-T stand for, added in 2022?
options: Engagement
Efficiency
Experience
Endorsement
questions.explain: The lesson explains the extra E added in 2022 is Experience, rewarding content from someone who has actually done the thing.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about whether Google penalizes AI-written content?
options: AI content is always penalized regardless of quality
False — Google penalizes thin, generic content, not content for being AI-written
AI content ranks higher automatically
Google bans all AI content from its index
questions.explain: The lesson states AI-written content is not penalized for being AI; the risk is thin, generic, mass-produced content with little value.

questions.q: What realistic timeline does the lesson give for meaningful SEO results?
options: 1-2 weeks
1-3 months
4-12 months
2-3 years
questions.explain: The lesson cites a 4-12 month window for meaningful SEO results, describing it as slow then compounding.

questions.q: What is the local pack (also called the map pack or 3-pack)?
options: A paid advertising bundle for local businesses
The boxed cluster of usually three local businesses, shown with a map, at the top of local-intent searches
A set of three keywords every page should target
A Google subscription tier for salons
questions.explain: The lesson defines the local pack as the top-of-page block of typically three local businesses shown with a map.

questions.q: Which two of Google's three local ranking factors are mostly within a business's control?
options: Relevance and prominence
Distance and relevance
Distance and prominence
Proximity and intent
questions.explain: The Local SEO lesson states businesses mostly control relevance and prominence but not distance.

questions.q: What does 'zero-click search' mean in the AEO/GEO context?
options: A search that returns no results
A search blocked by an ad blocker
A search answered on-screen so the user never clicks through to a website
A search performed without typing
questions.explain: The AEO/GEO lesson defines a zero-click search as one answered on-screen so the user never visits a website.

questions.q: In an AI voice agent, what is 'hallucination'?
options: When the agent transfers a call to a human
When the agent confidently makes up a wrong answer
When two callers hear different voices
When the agent records a message
questions.explain: The AI Voice lesson defines hallucination as an AI confidently making up a wrong answer.

questions.q: Which practice both Google's policies and the FTC's 2024 rule push against in reviews?
options: Asking every customer for a public review
Responding to negative reviews calmly
Review gating and suppression of negative reviews
Mentioning the stylist in a reply
questions.explain: The Reviews lesson explains review gating and suppression violate Google policy and the FTC's 2024 rule.

questions.q: What does the lesson identify as the #1 Google Business Profile local-pack ranking factor?
options: Number of photos uploaded
The primary category
Length of the business description
Having a booking button
questions.explain: The GBP lesson identifies the primary category as the #1 local pack ranking factor.

questions.q: Of the four classic search-intent types, which describes a searcher who wants to act now (e.g., 'book gel manicure downtown')?
options: Informational
Navigational
Commercial
Transactional
questions.explain: The SEO lesson classifies 'book/price/near me' act-now queries as transactional intent.

questions.q: What is a 'citation' in local SEO?
options: A backlink from a high-authority news site
Any place online where a business's NAP appears, such as Yelp or Apple Maps
A legal warning from Google about policy violations
A footnote in a blog post linking to the business
questions.explain: The Local SEO lesson defines a citation as any online place where a business's NAP (Name, Address, Phone) appears.

tracks.title: Discovery
tracks.blurb: Zoca's marketing engine: a real SEO website, local rankings, AI-search visibility, an optimised Google profile, and the leads it all drives.

modules.title: What Discovery is — the digital-marketing agent

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is the real starting point of Discovery?
options: Google Business Profile management
Keyword analysis — what people search and the demand behind it
Building the website
Replying to reviews
questions.explain: The 'UNLEARN THIS' callout says GBP is downstream of keywords; Discovery starts from keyword analysis and demand.

questions.q: How does Discovery fit into Zoca's three-agent model and packaging?
options: It is optional and only included in the full suite
It is sold only as a standalone product
It is mandatory and part of every combination — the wedge
It can be skipped if the customer buys Bookings
questions.explain: Discovery is in every combination — it's mandatory and is the wedge; there is no standalone Front Desk or Bookings.

questions.q: What are Discovery's three SEO pillars?
options: Local SEO, Website SEO, and AI search
Reviews, Photos, and Posts
Email, SMS, and Social
Paid ads, Organic, and Referral
questions.explain: The lesson defines the three pillars as Local SEO, Website SEO, and AI search.

questions.q: When a customer buys more than one agent, in what fixed order are they onboarded?
options: Front Desk → Bookings → Discovery
Bookings → Discovery → Front Desk
Discovery → Front Desk → Bookings
Discovery → Bookings → Front Desk
questions.explain: The 'GOOD TO KNOW' callout states the fixed order is Discovery → Bookings → Front Desk, because Front Desk needs scheduling context.

modules.title: Local SEO — getting found where customers search

questions.q: In the correct order, what are the five steps of the keyword pipeline?
options: Demand → Searches → Relevance → Selection → Competitor
Searches → Demand → Relevance → Competitor → Selection
Relevance → Searches → Demand → Competitor → Selection
Searches → Competitor → Demand → Relevance → Selection
questions.explain: The lesson lists the pipeline as Searches, Demand, Relevance, Competitor, Selection — in that order.

questions.q: How should a salon's primary Google category be chosen?
options: By a gut guess about what the business 'is'
By whichever service has the highest price
From impressions, demand, and competition data
Always 'hair salon' for any hair-and-nails salon
questions.explain: The 'DON'T ASSUME' callout says pick the primary category from impressions, demand, and competition — never from a gut guess.

questions.q: What is the difference between branded and non-branded keywords?
options: Branded contain the business or chain name; non-branded describe the service
Branded describe the service; non-branded contain the business name
Branded are paid ads; non-branded are organic
Branded are local; non-branded are hyperlocal
questions.explain: Branded keywords contain the business/chain name (e.g. 'VLCC near me'); non-branded describe the service (e.g. 'hair salon near me').

questions.q: On the Map View, how is rank shown and why are dense scans limited to about 3 per day?
options: A 5×5 grid; limited because of monthly billing caps
A 7×7 geo-grid over ~3 miles; each scan is 49 live Google queries
A single citywide pin; limited by Google account suspension risk
A 10×10 grid; limited because each scan emails the owner
questions.explain: The 'ON THE SCREEN' callout describes a 7×7 geo-grid over ~3 miles, with dense scans limited to ~3/day because each is 49 live Google queries.

modules.title: Website & content — the SEO site that sells for you

questions.q: What are the two calls to action that every Discovery-generated site carries?
options: Email and Directions
Subscribe and Share
Call and Book
Quote and Chat
questions.explain: The lesson states every site carries two CTAs: Call and Book.

questions.q: When does the generated website actually go live?
options: The instant it is generated in the demo
When the trial starts
After the first blog publishes
Only once the owner buys a custom domain
questions.explain: The 'HONESTY NOTE' clarifies the site goes live when the trial starts, not the moment it's generated.

questions.q: Why are Discovery's blogs formatted as questions and answers?
options: It is purely a stylistic preference
It makes blogs shorter and cheaper to produce
Q&A is the format Google and AI engines pull from for specific questions
It avoids any AI-content penalties
questions.explain: The 'GOOD TO KNOW' callout says the Q&A/FAQ format is strategic — it's what Google and AI engines pull from when someone asks a specific question.

questions.q: What happens to a Discovery website when the salon's services change?
options: The owner must manually rebuild each page
The site rebuilds itself to match (a 'website flip')
Nothing — the site is static once published
The whole site is taken offline until re-approved
questions.explain: The auto-rebuild section says the site rebuilds to match when services change — a 'website flip' — so the owner never updates pages manually.

modules.title: AI search (AEO/GEO) — being the salon the AI recommends

questions.q: What is the most important distinction to get right about AI search?
options: You hold a numbered position like 'position 3'
There is no ranking — only whether you're recommended and cited
Rankings matter more than mentions
Only paid placement gets you recommended
questions.explain: The lesson stresses there is no 'ranking' in AI search — it's about mentions and citations, not a position number.

questions.q: Which four AI engines are active in the Run Audit today?
options: ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overview, and Perplexity
ChatGPT, Claude, Bing, and Siri
Gemini, Perplexity, Alexa, and Copilot
ChatGPT, Grok, Google AI Overview, and Yelp
questions.explain: The lesson lists the four active engines as ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overview, and Perplexity.

questions.q: What does the AEO score measure, and on what scale?
options: Number of leads, scored 0–100
Profile completeness, scored high/medium/low
How strongly the business shows up in AI answers, scored 0–10
Competitor count, scored 1–5 stars
questions.explain: The AEO score measures how strongly the business shows up in AI answers, scored 0 to 10.

questions.q: How is Zoca positioned relative to the enterprise tool Profound?
options: Zoca resells Profound to small businesses
Zoca does for small businesses what Profound does for enterprise
Profound is a generic SEO agency to avoid comparing to
Zoca is built on Profound's API
questions.explain: The lesson frames Zoca as doing for small businesses what Profound does for enterprise companies like Salesforce and Ramp.

modules.title: Google Business Profile — the front door to local search

questions.q: Why must GBP verification be qualified early in the conversation?
options: Verification costs the owner extra money
An unverified profile breaks the overview screen and disables features
Google bans unverified businesses from search
Verification is only needed for the website, not the listing
questions.explain: The objection callout states an unverified profile breaks the overview screen and disables features, so it's a hard dependency to qualify early.

questions.q: How are collected reviews gated before going public?
options: All reviews auto-publish immediately
Reviews under 4 stars are held internally; 5-star/strong ones publish to the website and GBP
Only reviews left via QR code are published
The owner must manually publish every review
questions.explain: The 'HOW REVIEWS ARE GATED' callout: anything under 4 stars is held internally, while 5-star/strong reviews publish to the website and GBP.

questions.q: On the Photos screen, which three slots does Google score the profile on?
options: Logo, Cover, and Exterior
Logo, Interior, and Staff
Cover, Menu, and Products
Exterior, Interior, and Team
questions.explain: The 'ON THE SCREEN' callout names three photo slots Google scores you on: Logo, Cover, and Exterior.

questions.q: What is described as the single biggest ranking signal on the profile?
options: The number of photos uploaded
Hours accuracy
The primary category
The website link
questions.explain: The lesson states the primary category is the single biggest ranking signal (with hours accuracy as the top trust signal).

modules.title: Leads & reporting — sell the visible work, not a number

questions.q: What are the four statuses an enquiry can carry in the leads surface?
options: New, Contacted, Won, Lost
Booked, Not booked, Unresponsive, Duplicate
Hot, Warm, Cold, Dead
Open, Pending, Closed, Spam
questions.explain: The lesson lists the four lead statuses as Booked, Not booked, Unresponsive, and Duplicate.

questions.q: What is the central reframe of this lesson?
options: Promise a guaranteed monthly lead count
Sell the visible marketing work that produces leads, not a lead-prediction number
Focus the demo entirely on the leads list
Only sell the audit, never the dashboards
questions.explain: The big reframe is to sell the visible marketing work that produces leads, never a lead-prediction number.

questions.q: Where do abandoned booking leads from the Front Desk product appear?
options: Only inside the Front Desk product
They are discarded if not completed
In the Discovery leads surface
In a separate billing report
questions.explain: The lesson explains abandoned leads captured by Front Desk surface in the Discovery leads view.

questions.q: On the Overview tab, why does 'Reviews consistency' measure the percent of weeks with a new review rather than a lifetime total?
options: Because lifetime totals are hard to compute
Because Google rewards velocity, not a lifetime total
Because owners prefer weekly numbers
Because it limits Google API calls
questions.explain: The 'ON THE SCREEN' callout says Reviews consistency is the % of weeks with at least one new review because Google rewards velocity, not a lifetime total.

questions.q: Discovery is best described as Zoca's 'wedge.' What does that mean?
options: The most expensive, highest-commitment product
An optional add-on for existing customers
The lowest-commitment entry product that leads customers toward the rest of Zoca
A product that requires switching booking platforms
questions.explain: Discovery is the wedge: the lowest-commitment entry product (no booking switch) and the on-ramp to everything else.

questions.q: Which statement about AI search is correct?
options: Businesses are ranked at numbered positions
It's about being recommended and cited, not a position number
Only ChatGPT is measured
Citations never reveal competitors
questions.explain: AI search has no ranking — it's about mentions and citations, including which competitors got cited.

questions.q: How does Discovery select keywords?
options: A fixed flat list of a few keywords
By the full service catalog, measuring demand and qualifying by opportunity
Only branded keywords
Whatever the owner types in manually
questions.explain: Discovery looks at the full service catalog, measures demand, and qualifies services by opportunity — not a fixed flat list.

questions.q: What two CTAs appear on every Discovery website?
options: Call and Book
Map and Menu
Email and Subscribe
Review and Share
questions.explain: Every generated site carries both a Call and a Book button.

questions.q: What is E-E-A-T?
options: A pricing tier for Discovery plans
Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness — a content-quality framework
The four AI engines audited
The four lead statuses
questions.explain: E-E-A-T is Google's content-quality framework — Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, Trustworthiness — influencing both SEO and AI recommendations.

questions.q: Why is the Brain described as the 'moat' for AI recommendations?
options: It stores billing and payment data
It is a fixed keyword list
It holds genuinely unique business facts that keep content unique and grounded
It blocks competitors from being cited
questions.explain: The Brain stores genuinely unique business facts that keep content unique and grounded — exactly what gets a business recommended.

questions.q: Roughly how many blogs does the content engine publish by default, and how is it framed?
options: 5 per week, fixed
1 per day, fixed
~2 per week, configurable
10 per month, fixed
questions.explain: The default is ~2 blogs per week, presented as configurable — don't quote a fixed '5/week'.

questions.q: When a prospect asks 'how many leads will I get?', what is the recommended response?
options: Promise a specific monthly number
Refuse to give a number and redirect to the visible work and where they stand today
Quote the competitor's lead count
Estimate based on their review count
questions.explain: The lesson advises not to promise a number and to redirect to the visible work on the dashboard and where they stand today.

tracks.title: Front Desk
tracks.blurb: Zoe, the AI front desk that answers calls and messages, books appointments, and recovers leads who almost booked.

modules.title: What Zoe does — the AI receptionist on every call

questions.q: What is one of the things Zoe will explicitly NOT do?
options: Answer inbound calls 24/7
Collect a payment or take a deposit / card
Recognize returning clients by phone
Detect and filter spam
questions.explain: Zoe never collects payment or takes a deposit/card; the salon takes payment its normal way.

questions.q: How does Zoe recognize a returning client?
options: By asking the caller to state their name
By a downloaded client app
By the phone number they're calling from, matched to the client list
By voice recognition of the caller
questions.explain: Returning callers are matched on the phone number they're calling from, pulled from the salon's client list and booking history.

questions.q: How does Zoe's spam shield actually work?
options: It blocks junk calls before they ring, using a caller-reputation database
It answers, then tags very short calls and obvious robocalls as spam after the call
It forwards all suspicious calls to a human
It requires callers to pass a verification challenge first
questions.explain: The spam shield is post-call tagging of very short calls and obvious robocalls, not a pre-answer wall or third-party reputation database.

questions.q: About how long does a standard booking call with Zoe typically run?
options: 60-120 seconds
10-20 seconds
4-5 minutes
15-30 minutes
questions.explain: A standard booking call runs about 60-120 seconds; a quick hours question is 30-60 seconds and a messy reschedule can take 4-5 minutes.

modules.title: Booking & platforms — Zoe books into YOUR calendar

questions.q: What is the core differentiator of how Zoe handles bookings?
options: She texts the caller a booking link to complete later
She only works with Calendly
She writes the appointment into the salon's existing scheduler, live on the call
She emails the salon to enter the booking manually
questions.explain: Zoe writes the appointment end-to-end into the scheduler the salon already runs on, live on the call.

questions.q: Which two platforms are described as TRUE integrations through the salon's own account?
options: Booksy and Vagaro
Square and Mindbody
Fresha and GlossGenius
Zoca Scheduling and Boulevard
questions.explain: Square and Mindbody are true integrations via the salon's own account; Booksy, Vagaro, Fresha, and GlossGenius use the secure-assistant approach.

questions.q: Why does Zoe book without collecting a deposit or card on the call?
options: Because the schedulers don't support deposits
It's a deliberate feature so most bookings land confirmed instead of stuck awaiting payment
Because deposits are illegal over the phone
Because she can't access the salon's deposit settings
questions.explain: Deposits-off is deliberate; with no payment step to stall on, most Zoe bookings land confirmed and the salon's deposit settings stay untouched.

questions.q: What is the correct, customer-safe way to describe how Zoe connects to Booksy, Vagaro, Fresha, and GlossGenius?
options: An official API partnership
A reverse-engineered workaround
A secure automated assistant set up on the account using the salon's login
A manual data export each morning
questions.explain: The honest framing is a secure automated assistant on the account using the login; never say official API partnership, hacky, or workaround.

modules.title: Telephony & setup — the number, forwarding, and going live

questions.q: Who provides and pays for Zoe's dedicated phone number?
options: The salon, as a monthly add-on
Zoca provides and pays for it, and the owner can pick the area code
The salon's existing carrier
Google, via the Business Profile
questions.explain: Zoca provisions and pays for a US/Canada number, and the owner can choose the area code so it feels local.

questions.q: How does the salon keep its existing number while using Zoe?
options: By forwarding its existing line to Zoe's number
By instant self-serve porting of the number to Zoca
By replacing all signage with the new number
By using two separate phones at the front desk
questions.explain: The salon forwards its existing line to Zoe's number via a guided wizard; a true self-serve port-in is only on the roadmap.

questions.q: What does Zoe's transfer/handoff capability look like today?
options: A warm transfer to multiple destinations
A cold transfer to one destination during transfer hours
No transfer is possible at all
An automatic transfer to a call center
questions.explain: Today it's a cold transfer to one destination per salon during transfer hours; warm transfer and multiple destinations are on the roadmap.

questions.q: How long does Zoe's guided onboarding take, and how many steps does it have?
options: A multi-day IT project across 20 steps
About 5 minutes, fully self-serve, 3 steps
About 45 minutes (rarely over an hour), 10 steps
About 2 hours, 7 steps
questions.explain: Setup is a guided ~45-minute, 10-step onboarding ending with a free test call and go-live.

modules.title: Training & memory — teaching Zoe to sound like your salon

questions.q: Which two Training tab sections are REQUIRED to go live?
options: QnAs and Policies
Business Profile and Services
Custom Instructions and QnAs
Services and Policies
questions.explain: Business Profile and Services are the two required-to-go-live sections; QnAs, Policies, and Custom Instructions fine-tune her.

questions.q: How many voices can the owner choose from for Zoe?
options: Four (Eryn, Vexa, Mark, Jessica)
Two (male and female)
Unlimited via voice cloning
Six, one per salon type
questions.explain: The owner picks one of four voices (Eryn, Vexa, Mark, Jessica); there is no voice cloning.

questions.q: How does the 'Questions from calls' Brain loop work?
options: Zoe mines transcripts and invents memories automatically
Zoe surfaces questions she couldn't answer, and the owner's answer becomes knowledge
An AI auto-answers every gap without owner input
The owner must re-record the whole Training tab weekly
questions.explain: Zoe surfaces questions she couldn't fully answer; the owner answers, and that answer becomes permanent knowledge, keeping the owner in control.

questions.q: What is Configs, the flagship upcoming feature?
options: A live feature today for warm transfers
A way to clone the owner's voice
Rules so Zoe acts more like the owner, e.g. offering an on-the-spot discount (not live yet)
A second calendar for Zoe to manage
questions.explain: Configs (~1-2 months, flagship) will let Zoe act like the owner, headlined by on-the-spot discounting, but it isn't live and shouldn't be demoed as such.

modules.title: Dashboard & lead recovery — the proof and the payoff

questions.q: Which dashboard tab serves as the inbox of every call and text Zoe handled?
options: Overview
Bookings
Activity
Analytics
questions.explain: The Activity feed is the inbox; there's no separate Inbox tab, and it shows transcripts, AI summaries, and recordings.

questions.q: What does L2B (Lead-to-Booking) do?

modules.title: Brain — what it is & why it matters

questions.q: What is the Brain, in one line?
options: A shared industry database every Zoca business contributes facts to
A per-business memory layer storing owner-approved facts that grounds every Zoca AI
A standalone chatbot that replaces the front-desk phone line
A generic AI writing tool like ChatGPT for marketing copy

questions.q: Why does fixing one fact in the Brain improve every Zoca tool at once?
options: Because each tool keeps its own copy that syncs nightly
Because the owner manually pushes updates to each AI
Because all five Zoca AIs read from the same Brain
Because only the website and Front Desk share facts
questions.explain: All five Zoca AIs read from the same Brain, so correcting one fact makes every tool better at once.

questions.q: Which is one of the three foundation principles of how the Brain works?

Per-business ownership — a Brain belongs to one business and is never shared
Facts are auto-confirmed without owner review to save time
The Brain stays fixed and never changes after setup
questions.explain: Per-business ownership means a Brain belongs to one business and is never pooled or shared.

questions.q: According to the lesson, can owners control whether a fact is used per-tool today (e.g., on calls but not the blog)?
options: Yes, per-surface control is fully available now

Yes, but only for pricing facts
Only staff accounts can set per-tool rules

Validate
Preview
Memory History

options: Approve, Pause, Archive, Delete
Confirm, Refine, Edit, Reject

questions.q: What does the Preview tab let an owner do?

Type a customer question and see the exact grounded answer with citations to the facts used
Bulk-import an FAQ list
Compare their Brain to a competitor's
questions.explain: Preview lets you type any customer question and see the exact grounded answer with citations to the Brain facts it used.

questions.q: Why do compliance-minded buyers care about Memory History?
options: It hides facts from staff members
It auto-deletes old facts after 30 days
It's a complete, dated, attributed, exportable audit trail of every fact with one-click restore
It blocks the AI from answering until reviewed

Your website, Google Business Profile, past call transcripts, and existing Zoca data
Generated blog and social posts
Competitor websites and Yelp reviews only

Flags the conflict and offers a three-way choice: replace, keep both, or cancel

$50 per month per business
$100 per month per location
There is no cap

Validate → Memory History → Canvas → Preview

Showing the $50 cost cap first

Question Bank
Preview

Read, Write, Confirm, and Memory
Sales, HR, Legal, and Finance
questions.explain: The specialists cover Scheduling, Discovery/marketing, Front Desk, and Support.

questions.q: Which of these is a READ action?
options: "Reply to my latest review."
"Post an update about my new summer color package."
"Pull up everyone who hasn't booked in 90 days."
"Add a pedicure to this booking and send a deposit link."
questions.explain: Pulling up clients who haven't booked fetches data without changing anything, so it is a read.

questions.q: How does Command Center's memory operate?
options: Per user and reset each session
Per business and shared across the business
Global across all Zoca businesses
Only retained for 24 hours
questions.explain: Memory is per business and shared across the business so it stays consistent regardless of who uses it.

questions.q: How are a business's multiple locations handled in Command Center?
options: Each location needs a separate login and chat
One conversation handles all locations without switching and starting over
Only the primary location is supported
Locations must be merged into one before use
questions.explain: One conversation handles all locations; the owner can ask about one then another in the same chat.

questions.q: What is the relationship between Command Center and Zoca's Brain?
options: Command Center can only read from the Brain
The Brain is a separate product Command Center cannot access
It is a two-way link: Command Center reads from and writes to the Brain
Command Center replaces the Brain entirely
questions.explain: The connection is two-way: it reads Brain facts to ground answers and writes new facts other tools can use.

tracks.title: Onboarding
tracks.blurb: How a new salon goes from sign-up to live: the flow, the trial/contract/card step, and the per-platform journeys.

modules.title: Onboarding — the flow

questions.q: How is Zoca onboarding delivered to a prospect?
options: As a public self-serve sign-up they complete alone
As an assisted, desktop-first setup run with the prospect on a screen-share
As a downloadable mobile app installed before the demo
As an emailed login the owner figures out on their own
questions.explain: Onboarding is an assisted, desktop-first session run with the prospect on a screen-share, not a public self-serve sign-up.

questions.q: In what fixed order are the three AI agents introduced during agent setup?
options: Front Desk, Bookings, Discovery
Bookings, Discovery, Front Desk
Discovery, Bookings, Front Desk
Discovery, Front Desk, Bookings
questions.explain: The agents are introduced one at a time in the fixed order Discovery, then Bookings, then Front Desk.

questions.q: Where do a salon's services come from during onboarding?
options: They are imported automatically from the salon's current booking link and confirmed on a review screen
The owner retypes every service and price from scratch
They are copied from the salon's Google Business Profile
An AE enters them manually after the call ends
questions.explain: Services are imported automatically from the current booking link, then confirmed on a review-services screen before the website builds.

questions.q: What are the three sections of onboarding?
options: Discovery, Bookings, and Front Desk
Platform setup, agent setup, and formalities
Audit, demo, and migration
Sign-in, payment, and go-live
questions.explain: Onboarding is organized into three sections: platform setup, per-agent setup, and formalities.

modules.title: Onboarding — trial, contract & card

questions.q: How long is the free trial, and when does the first charge land?
options: 14 days, charged on the first day
30 days, charged immediately
7 days, charged only after the trial ends
7 days, charged at the moment the card is added
questions.explain: The trial is 7 days and the first charge auto-bills only after the trial ends, like Netflix.

questions.q: Which payment methods are supported to start the trial?
options: Card only; PayPal and Apple Pay are not supported
Card, PayPal, and Apple Pay
PayPal or Apple Pay only
Bank transfer or card
questions.explain: A valid, funded card is required to start the trial; PayPal and Apple Pay are not supported.

questions.q: What happens to the contract when a business adds more agents later?
options: A brand-new contract must be signed and a new card added
The existing contract is augmented automatically with no re-signing and the same card
The trial restarts from day one
The business must book an offboarding call first
questions.explain: Adding agents later augments the same one-per-business contract automatically with no re-signing and the same card on file.

questions.q: How does a customer cancel during the trial?
options: By emailing a cancellation request
By letting the card expire on its own
By clicking a single cancel button in settings
By booking an offboarding call rather than flipping a switch
questions.explain: Cancellation isn't one click; it requires booking an offboarding call so there's a human conversation first.

modules.title: Onboarding — platform journeys

questions.q: How many platform journeys are there, and what decides which one a prospect lands in?
options: Three journeys, decided by their plan tier
Five journeys, decided by the platform they run today
Five journeys, decided by how much they pay
Three journeys, decided by their location
questions.explain: There are five platform journeys, and the prospect's current booking platform determines which one they land in.

questions.q: What does the secure automated assistant do on the salon's platform?
options: It edits and updates the salon's existing system
It deletes the old platform after migrating
It reads their information read-only without changing their existing system
It charges the salon a connection fee
questions.explain: The secure automated assistant signs in to read the salon's current data read-only and never changes their existing system.

questions.q: How does pricing differ between the platform journeys?
options: There is no price difference; the journey only changes the setup steps
The flagship migration costs the most
Direct connection is cheapest
The secure automated assistant adds a surcharge
questions.explain: There is no price difference between journeys; the journey changes only the setup, not the bill.

questions.q: What does the flagship migration journey do?
options: Keeps the salon entirely on their old platform
Reads data read-only without moving anything
Connects two systems but changes nothing
Moves the salon fully onto Zoca's own bookings and payments
questions.explain: The flagship migration moves the salon fully onto Zoca's own bookings and payments as the end-state.

questions.q: How should you pitch Zoca onboarding in one line?
options: "Sign up online and explore on your own."
"Three steps, one screen-share, and you're live."
"Download the app and we'll call you later."
"Pay first, then we set everything up."
questions.explain: The flow doc pitches onboarding as "Three steps, one screen-share, and you're live."

questions.q: Roughly how long does getting a salon live with website, bookings, and AI receptionist take?
options: A full working day
About three business days
Well under an hour
Around two to three hours
questions.explain: The whole setup comes together in well under an hour.

questions.q: During Front Desk setup, what does the prospect do?
options: Connect platform, set up number, choose voice, set call forwarding, and run a test call
Only confirm services and prices
Import their booking link and build a website
E-sign the contract and add a card
questions.explain: Front Desk has the prospect connect the platform, set up a number, choose a voice, set call forwarding, and run a live test call.

questions.q: Why is the card-on-file step framed "like Netflix"?
options: Because Zoca streams training videos
Because the trial includes free movies
Because billing is handled by Netflix
Because you put a card down, get a free week, and aren't charged until it's up
questions.explain: The Netflix framing means a card on file starts a free week with no charge until the trial ends, and you can cancel.

questions.q: If a payment fails after the trial, what happens?
options: Access is cut off instantly
There's a short grace period to fix it before functionality closes
The trial automatically restarts
A second card is charged automatically
questions.explain: A failed payment triggers a short grace period to resolve it before access closes.

questions.q: What kind of business is onboarding built for today?
options: Multi-location chains only
Franchises with shared billing
Solo and single-location businesses (multiple staff are fine)
Online-only businesses with no storefront
questions.explain: Onboarding is built for solo and single-location businesses; multiple staff are fine but multiple locations aren't yet.

questions.q: Why must onboarding be confirmed on the current environment before a live setup?
options: Because the newest version lives in the demo/sandbox environment and production can lag
Because production is always more up to date
Because the prospect chooses the environment
Because pricing differs by environment
questions.explain: The newest version lives in the demo/sandbox environment and production can lag, so confirm the current environment first.

questions.q: Where are the salon's card details stored?
options: Directly by Zoca on its own servers
By the salon's current booking platform
By Zoca's billing provider, not by Zoca directly
Only on the owner's local device
questions.explain: Card details are stored by Zoca's billing provider, not held by Zoca directly.

tracks.title: Selling Zoca
tracks.blurb: How to actually sell the suite: the master objection bank, how the beauty business really works, and how the sales team is organised.

modules.title: Welcome to Zoca & the dream

questions.q: What is the one-line definition of Zoca a rep should lead with?
options: An AI agency for small businesses
The marketing + voice platform for hyperlocal beauty and wellness businesses
The future of beauty SaaS
A voice tool with bolt-on SEO
questions.explain: The lesson says every word of "the marketing + voice platform for hyperlocal beauty and wellness businesses" is load-bearing, and rejects "an AI agency" or "the future of beauty."

questions.q: A prospect has no laptop or iPad anywhere in the shop. What is the correct move?
options: Tell them they don't qualify and end the call
Onboard anyway over the phone
Get a laptop or iPad to the front desk first, then onboard
Refer them to a competitor
questions.explain: A laptop or iPad in the shop is the only hard rule; the move is to get a device first, then onboard, not to turn the prospect away.

questions.q: A solo operator at $40K with one location and no staff is best described as:
options: Lower-fit, not a no
Disqualified from buying
Best-fit, move fast
Outside the vertical entirely
questions.explain: The lesson frames this owner as lower-fit, not a no; the wins are smaller and slower, but they're still sellable with honest expectation-setting.

questions.q: A prospect cites $249/month from an old product doc. What should the rep do?
options: Honor the $249 since it's documented
Treat it as the official price
Quote $290 instead
Reject it as stale, flag it to RevOps, and quote the placeholder of record
questions.explain: $179/$249/$269/$279/$290 are all stale; reps reject any stale number, flag it, and quote the placeholder since pricing is pending final confirmation.

modules.title: The four leaks

questions.q: Which leak does the lesson call the single most leveraged, because the customer already chose the business?
options: New bookings / visibility gap
Missed inbound calls
Mid-booking drop-off (the Black Box)
First-timer churn
questions.explain: Mid-booking drop-off (the Black Box) is the single most leveraged leak because the intent already happened; the customer just didn't finish.

questions.q: What are the four leak benchmark numbers a rep should memorize?
questions.explain: The spine of every discovery call is 37 (visibility), 22 (missed calls), 31 (mid-booking drop), 52 (first-timer churn).

questions.q: An owner says they don't have a marketing problem. The lesson's framing is that the owner:
options: Has a demand problem the rep must fix first
Should be told they're wrong about marketing
Has a capture problem, not a demand problem
Is not a fit for Zoca
questions.explain: Demand already exists; owners have a capture problem (short on time and skill to capture demand), not a demand problem.

questions.q: When an owner mentions the agency they currently pay, what should the rep do?
options: Bash the agency to win the deal
Reframe why an agency can't work in real time across locations, without attacking the owner's judgment
Refuse to discuss the agency
Promise to beat the agency's price with a stale number
questions.explain: The lesson bans bashing the agency since the owner chose it; reframe why a good past decision no longer fits, without insulting their judgment.

modules.title: Our ICP — best-fit, not a hard no

questions.q: How does the lesson define "ICP" for Zoca?
options: A gate that turns away customers who don't meet the bar
A best-fit, targeting and expectation-setting tool, not a gate
A list of businesses we refuse to serve
A hard revenue floor every customer must clear
questions.explain: ICP is the best-fit picture, a targeting and expectation-setting tool, explicitly not a gate that turns paying customers away.

questions.q: Where do tattoo, piercing, and permanent makeup studios fall?
options: Outside the vertical, refuse them
Low-ticket, excluded categories
In-vertical, best-fit beauty categories
Verify with Sales Ops before selling
questions.explain: Tattoo, piercing, and permanent makeup are in-vertical, best-fit beauty categories, sold like any other beauty shop.

questions.q: What is the decided lead-prediction signal for a best-fit shop?
options: At least ~60 new leads over the next six months
At least 100 leads per month
Pending a Sales Ops decision
At least $100K in revenue
questions.explain: Best-fit shops are projected to generate at least ~60 new leads over the next six months; this is decided, not pending Sales Ops.

questions.q: A dentist with budget wants to buy Zoca. The correct approach is to:
options: Decline because they're outside beauty
Sell as if the product is fully tuned for dental
Tell them they don't qualify
Be honest that the product is tuned for beauty so some category intelligence won't apply, name what still works, and let them decide
questions.explain: Beauty & wellness is the sharpest fit but not a wall; out-of-vertical owners are still sellable with honest expectation-setting, never refused.

modules.title: What we do — Discovery Neo & the agent architecture

questions.q: What two agents make up Discovery Neo, the product every new logo gets?
options: Discovery Agent and Front Desk Agent
Booking Agent and Loyalty Agent
Conversion Agent and Ads Agent
Front Desk Agent and Booking Agent
questions.explain: Discovery Neo bundles the Discovery Agent (marketing brain) and Front Desk Agent (voice brain), sold together as one product.

questions.q: What is the default operating mode for the agents?
options: Approve
Auto
Supervised
Manual
questions.explain: Supervised is the default: the agent acts on its own and surfaces the important decisions in the Content Queue; most customers stay there.

questions.q: How are the Loyalty and Conversion add-ons priced?
options: Both free with 2.7% per transaction
Loyalty $49/mo (500 SMS + 100 AI calls); Conversion $49/mo + 10% of recovered booking value
Loyalty $179/mo; Conversion $249/mo
Both bundled into the base plan at no cost
questions.explain: Loyalty is $49/mo including 500 SMS + 100 AI calls; Conversion is $49/mo + 10% of recovered booking value and requires B&P connected.

questions.q: When a prospect asks who provides the voice AI under the hood, the rep should say:
options: Name the third-party voice vendor
It's all built in house
We license it from a partner
We can't discuss it at all
questions.explain: The answer is "it's all built in house"; reps never name third-party voice vendors on customer calls.

modules.title: Why we win — positioning against everything else

questions.q: What does the lesson say is the most common alternative an owner is actually weighing?
options: A marketing/SEO agency
A deal platform like Groupon
A legacy booking platform with an AI plugin
Doing nothing and living with the leak
questions.explain: Doing nothing (living with the leak) is the most common alternative; selling against it means selling against inertia.

questions.q: The core reason Zoca leads cannot be Groupon leads is rooted in:
options: Search intent, branded vs. non-branded search
Zoca offering a bigger discount
Groupon's higher platform fees alone
Zoca being listed on Groupon too
questions.explain: Search intent decides everything: Groupon customers used a branded search, while Zoca leads searched non-branded service terms and pay full price.

questions.q: An owner says "We already pay GlossGenius, they have an AI thing now." The best move is to:
options: Tell them to rip out GlossGenius and replace it
Ask whether GlossGenius is doing their SEO and content, and clarify Zoca connects rather than replaces booking
Bash GlossGenius as a legacy tool
Concede they're already covered
questions.explain: The existing-vendor objection is usually partial coverage (booking) masquerading as full; find the gap and note Zoca connects to booking, not a rip-and-replace.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is Zoca's moat?
options: Lowest price in the market
The largest sales team
Building only for beauty and wellness, vertical depth a horizontal platform can't match
Owning the customer relationship like a deal platform
questions.explain: "Zoca only builds for beauty and wellness, that's the moat"; vertical depth is product depth a horizontal platform can't match.

modules.title: The Zoca values

questions.q: What is the correct public-facing contract phrasing per Value 04?
options: "No contracts"
"No long-term contracts"
"Zero-commitment"
"Cancel anytime, no agreement"
questions.explain: Say "no long-term contracts," never "no contracts" — we do sign service agreements at trial start.

questions.q: What was the root failure behind the April 2026 SDR incident in which 34 sales SMS reached paid customers?
options: An SDR was deliberately targeting paid accounts
A misapplied export filter that wasn't applied at send time, plus banned phrasing in the copy
The CRM crashed and resent old messages
Paid customers opted into the sales list by mistake
questions.explain: The exclusion filter was applied at list-prep rather than send time; the copy also carried Zoca branding and performance-shaming language.

questions.q: When running the six-value filter on a decision no policy covers, which two questions catch most bad decisions?
options: #5 (dreaming big) and #6
#3 (figure it out) and #4 (boring vs. bold)
#1 (does this serve the customer winning?) and #2 (am I being completely honest?)
#4 (the bold move) and #5 (betting on people)
questions.explain: Bad decisions almost always fail at #1 (customer winning) or #2 (honesty); most decisions resolve in the first two.

questions.q: Per the honesty rules, how should an AE describe Booking, Loyalty, and Ads Agents on a discovery call?
options: As live features included in the base bundle today
As Coming Soon upside, sold without a launch date
As features that ship next week if the prospect signs today
As permanently unavailable and not worth mentioning
questions.explain: Coming-Soon agents are sold as upside so owners see the roadmap, but never with a launch date.

modules.title: Integrations — we don't rip out your booking app

questions.q: As of May 2026, which booking platforms are the confirmed live integrations?
options: Booksy and Vagaro
GlossGenius and Fresha
Square and Acuity
MindBody and Schedulicity
questions.explain: GlossGenius and Fresha are the confirmed integrations today, with roughly four more near-live; confirm current status before promising a platform.

questions.q: How does Zoca handle payments relative to the booking platform?
options: Zoca processes all payments directly through its own rail
Zoca orchestrates — it triggers the booking platform's payment/deposit flow but never processes payments itself
Zoca replaces the booking platform's payment system entirely
Zoca routes payments through a generic CRM
questions.explain: Zoca orchestrates rather than processes: Front Desk Agent calls back into the booking platform's payment flow and confirms when paid.

questions.q: A prospect's booking platform isn't a live Zoca integration yet. What is the correct move?
options: Tell them the deal is dead and move on
Treat it as a migration/integration conversation — still a real deal, scope the setup honestly
Promise the integration ships next week
Refuse them unless they switch immediately
questions.explain: A not-yet-live platform is never a hard no — it becomes a migration conversation where you scope the setup honestly and let them decide.

questions.q: Across the integration landscape, what is the only true hard prerequisite for onboarding?
options: The prospect must already be on GlossGenius or Fresha
A laptop or iPad must be in the shop
The prospect must connect QuickBooks
The prospect must be a multi-location business
questions.explain: The only true hard prerequisite anywhere in onboarding is a laptop or iPad in the shop; everything else flexes.

modules.title: The qualifying call

questions.q: Why does the qualifying call save the revenue question for later rather than opening with it?
options: Revenue is irrelevant to fit
Owners get defensive when a stranger leads with revenue; by then location and staff answers have already revealed size
Reps aren't allowed to ask revenue at all
Revenue must be the last question of the call
questions.explain: Opening with revenue makes owners defensive; by the time you ask, the location and staff answers make the range question feel like normal scoping.

questions.q: What is the decided lead-prediction signal for healthy demand?
options: At least 100 leads per month
At least 60 leads over the next six months
At least 60 leads per month
Pending Sales Ops decision
questions.explain: The lead signal is decided: at least 60 leads over the next six months; thinner demand means slower, smaller wins, not a no.

questions.q: A single-location solo shop owner doing under $100K is on the call. How does the AE handle fit?
options: Disqualify them — they don't meet the revenue floor
Workable, lower-fit — still sellable with modest, honest expectations
Refuse and tell them to come back at $500K
Quote a discounted price to win them
questions.explain: Fit is best-fit not a hard no: a sub-$100K solo shop is workable lower-fit, still sellable with honest expectation-setting.

questions.q: When a prospect asks about add-on pricing, which statement is correct?
options: Loyalty Agent is free; Conversion Agent has no prerequisite
Conversion Agent is $49/mo + 10% of recovered value and requires Bookings & Payments connected
Ads Agent is $49/mo flat
Bookings & Payments costs $49/mo
questions.explain: Conversion is $49/mo + 10% of recovered value and requires B&P connected; B&P is free + 2.7%/txn, Loyalty is $49/mo, Ads pricing is TBD.

modules.title: The demo — canonical flow & dev controls

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Day 0 to Wk 3 toggle reveal in the demo?
options: To show the prospect a discount tier
To set honest expectations — the empty Day 0 dashboard first, then the populated Wk 3 destination
To demonstrate the billing cycle
To compare Zoca against an agency
questions.explain: Showing the empty Day 0 first then toggling to Wk 3 makes the slow start feel honest, preventing churn from customers expecting Wk 3 numbers on day one.

questions.q: If a prospect asks during the Test Call whether it's really AI, how should the AE answer?
options: Name the third-party voice vendor that powers it
Be honest that it's the Front Desk Agent, built in-house, without naming any vendor
Deny it's AI to keep the magic
Refuse to answer and move on
questions.explain: The AE says it's the Front Desk Agent built in-house and never names a third-party vendor.

questions.q: At roughly which point should the pricing reveal happen in the canonical 20-minute demo?
options: Minute 4, right after the opening
Minute 12, during the four promises
Near the very end (minute 17-18) after the gap and fixes are loaded
Before screen-sharing begins
questions.explain: Pricing is held to the end on purpose so the prospect has felt the gap and seen the fix before the number lands.

questions.q: What is the Dev panel and where does it exist?
options: A real customer-facing settings page in production
A sales-only toggle panel in the preview that renders any state on one link; it does not exist in production
The prospect's actual Google Business Profile editor
A billing console for managing subscriptions
questions.explain: The Dev panel is a sales tool that renders every dashboard state on one shared link; it is not a real-customer surface and isn't in production.

modules.title: Pricing, packaging, closing & billing

questions.q: How does the Zoca billing model handle a customer adding agents like Loyalty or Conversion later?
options: Each agent gets its own separate subscription and billing date
They join the same single subscription on the same billing cycle; renewals consolidate all active agents
A new subscription is created and the old one is cancelled
Adding an agent requires re-signing the contract
questions.explain: One subscription, one cycle: added agents join the same subscription, renewals consolidate them, and there are no per-agent subscriptions.

questions.q: When a customer upgrades from monthly to yearly, when does the upgrade take effect?
options: Only at the end of the current cycle, no other option
Only immediately, no other option
The customer chooses — at the end of the current cycle OR immediately — and lands on the subscription page
It always waits until the next calendar year
questions.explain: The upgrade is one-click and the customer chooses whether it applies at the end of the cycle or immediately, then lands on the subscription page.

questions.q: What happens financially when a customer downgrades by turning an agent off mid-cycle?
options: They get a prorated refund for the remainder of the cycle
There is no mid-cycle refund; the structure is unchanged and no new subscription is created
A new subscription is created at a lower rate
Cancellation is triggered automatically
questions.explain: Downgrade is right-sizing: no mid-cycle refund, structure unchanged, no new subscription — they stop paying for that agent at the next cycle.

questions.q: What is the correct stance on discounts and the setup fee?
options: AEs have a pricing floor they can discount down to
There is no AE discount floor; the annual rate is the discount, and the setup fee is waived only on annual
There is no setup fee at all
The setup fee is waived on monthly but charged on annual
questions.explain: There are no discounts beyond annual pricing — the annual rate is the discount — and the setup fee is waived only on the annual plan.

modules.title: Objection handling — the top plays

questions.q: Per Cole's rule, what is the correct first move when a prospect raises an objection?
options: Defend Zoca's position with data immediately
Concede the real point first, then redirect
Bulldoze past the legitimate part to keep momentum
Restate the price and go silent
questions.explain: Cole's rule is to concede the legitimate part of the objection first, then reframe — don't defend, don't bulldoze.

questions.q: When handling 'It's too expensive,' the leak-math reframe moves the conversation from the price of Zoca to what?
options: A competitor's lower price
A guaranteed ROI promise
The dollar cost of the prospect's own leaks (e.g., missed calls)
A discount you can offer
questions.explain: The leak-math reframe translates the monthly price into the cost of the prospect's missed calls/drop-offs using their own numbers; price stays firm.

questions.q: A prospect asks 'How do you rank on AI search?' What is the correct handling?
options: Quote a target ranking position you can hit in 30 days
Explain there is no ranking in AI search — it's about being recommended and cited
Promise top placement on ChatGPT and Gemini
Defer the question to engineering
questions.explain: It's a trick question: AI search recommends and cites, it doesn't rank. Recognizing this signals real understanding of GEO/AEO.

questions.q: Against 'What if the AI makes a mistake?', the recommended posture is to:
options: Promise the agent never makes mistakes
Concede it will make mistakes, then explain how they're contained (recorded, correctable, human fallback)
Argue every human receptionist is worse
Avoid the topic and pivot to pricing
questions.explain: Don't promise perfection — concede mistakes happen, then contain: every call recorded, correctable in 30 seconds, and human-routing fallback.

modules.title: Pipeline, systems & the dashboards you own

questions.q: How many deal stages does Zoca's pipeline use, and how many can a deal occupy at once?
options: 5 stages; a deal can span two
6 stages; a deal lives in exactly one at a time
7 stages; a deal lives in exactly one
6 stages; a deal can span two adjacent stages
questions.explain: Zoca runs 6 deal stages, and a deal sits in exactly one stage at a time.

questions.q: What does the 14-day stale-deal rule require?
options: Automatically close any deal older than 14 days
Give any deal untouched for 14 days a decision: re-engage with a concrete next step or move to Closed Lost with a reason
Move stale deals forward a stage to keep the forecast warm
Wait 14 more days before deciding
questions.explain: Any open deal with no movement for 14 days gets a decision — a concrete next step or Closed Lost with a logged reason — never a shrug.

questions.q: What must a Demo Completed deal's recap email contain, sent within 4 hours?
options: A second pitch and Coming Soon feature promises
The exact pricing the prospect agreed to verbally, plus pain, next step, and a missing-info ask
Marketing copy and 'no contracts' wording
Whatever pricing makes the deal easier to close
questions.explain: The 4-line recap is a record, not a pitch; it must carry the exact agreed pricing or you get disputes at month 2.

questions.q: A prospect asks for a lower price because 'every dollar counts.' The correct move is to:
options: Offer a small discount to close faster
Hold the price, reframe to leak math, and note the setup fee is waived on annual
Quote the monthly number as if it were a discount
Escalate to a manager for discount approval
questions.explain: Don't discount — hold price, reframe to leak math, and use the annual setup-fee waiver; discounting trains the prospect that price is negotiable.

modules.title: The Conversion Agent, the coming-soon agents & the flywheel

questions.q: What is the correct pricing for the Conversion Agent?
options: $49/mo flat, no transaction fee
$49/mo + 10% of recovered booking value, requires Bookings & Payments connected
Free monthly + 2.7% per transaction
Pricing TBD — never quote
questions.explain: Conversion Agent is $49/mo plus 10% of recovered booking value and requires B&P connected; you only pay when it saves a booking.

questions.q: How should you position the Booking, Loyalty, and Ads agents?
options: As shipping in Q3 with firm dates
As upside / 'on the roadmap,' never with launch dates
As fully live and included in the value math
As reasons to delay signing until they ship
questions.explain: Coming-soon agents are sold as upside, named because the prospect sees them in the sidebar, but never with a launch date.

questions.q: Which statement about Ashley is correct?
options: Ashley is a chatbot that answers questions
Ashley is an AI assistant search bar
Ashley is an AI account manager who reads the account and acts on it
Ashley is the human dedicated AM for $5K+ accounts
questions.explain: Ashley is an AI account manager — never a chatbot; she's trained on the account, acts, and replies in under 30 seconds.

questions.q: When a prospect asks the price of the Ads Agent, you should:
options: Quote a rough monthly fee to look prepared
Say pricing is still landing and will be published before launch — never improvise a number
Tell them it's free
Bundle it into the Conversion Agent price
questions.explain: Ads Agent pricing is TBD; never quote a number — say it's still landing and bundled annual customers get the launch deal automatically.

modules.title: The account-management lifecycle — handoff to renewal

questions.q: At what Annual Contract Value does account ownership split, and what are the two lanes?
options: $3K split: pod vs. self-serve
$5K split: under $5K = Customer Success Pod, $5K+ = dedicated named AM
$10K split: shared inbox vs. AM
$5K split: under $5K = dedicated AM, $5K+ = pod
questions.explain: The $5K ACV split is fixed: under $5K goes to the Customer Success Pod, $5K and above gets a dedicated named AM with proactive MBR outreach.

questions.q: What are the 4-hour and 24-hour clocks on Day 1 of the handoff?
options: First content posts in 4 hrs; first review in 24 hrs
Customer hears from us within 4 hrs of signing; the 8-item confirmation list is clean within 24 hrs
Refund window 4 hrs; cancellation window 24 hrs
Orientation in 4 hrs; MBR in 24 hrs
questions.explain: The customer must hear from us within 4 hours of signing; the 8-item confirmation list must be locked within 24 hours.

questions.q: In a churn-prevention call, what is the rule about discounts?
options: Offer a one-time discount to save the relationship
Never discount to save churn — use the honest 'pause and come back' path instead
Discount only for $5K+ accounts
Match any competitor's price
questions.explain: Never discount to save churn; it trains both sides badly and they churn at renewal anyway. The preserve-and-re-subscribe path works better.

questions.q: When a wrong-fit solo owner asks to cancel and the volume for real lift was never there, what is the correct reframe?
options: Fix-it: demonstrate a config fix on the call
Value: open the MBR panel and show six months of numbers
Let-them-go: honestly recommend they cancel and leave the door open
Cash flow: offer to revisit in 30 days
questions.explain: The let-them-go reframe applies to a wrong-fit ICP — recommend cancellation honestly and note the file; these customers most often return later.

questions.q: What is the ONLY hard rule in the entire Zoca curriculum?
options: The prospect must be in beauty & wellness
A laptop or iPad must be in the shop (onboarding/demo can't run without it)
The prospect must have 60+ leads per month
The prospect cannot be using Vagaro
questions.explain: A laptop or iPad in the shop is the single hard rule — onboarding can't run without it. Everything else flexes under best-fit framing.

questions.q: How should a rep treat an out-of-vertical prospect (e.g., a dental office or gym)?
options: Disqualify them — they're not ICP
Refuse the sale and refer them elsewhere
Be honest the product is tuned for beauty and some category intelligence won't apply, then let them decide — still sellable
Tell them they don't qualify
questions.explain: ICP is best-fit, not a hard no. Beauty & wellness is the sharpest fit, but out-of-vertical prospects are still sellable with honest expectation-setting.

questions.q: What are the four leaks Zoca closes?
options: Pricing, payroll, payments, taxes
New bookings/visibility, missed calls, mid-booking drop-off, first-timer churn
Reviews, refunds, no-shows, deposits
SEO, ads, social, email
questions.explain: The four leaks are new bookings/visibility, missed calls, mid-booking drop-off, and first-timer churn — consistent across the curriculum.

questions.q: What does every new logo buy, and how is it framed?
options: All five agents on separate subscriptions
Discovery Agent + Front Desk Agent bundled as 'Discovery Neo'
Only the Front Desk Agent
Discovery Neo plus a mandatory Conversion Agent
questions.explain: Discovery Agent + Front Desk Agent ship together as Discovery Neo; Conversion, Booking, Loyalty, and Ads are add-ons/coming-soon.

questions.q: Which add-on pricing statement is correct?
options: Bookings & Payments is $49/mo flat
Loyalty Agent is $49/mo and includes 500 SMS + 100 AI calls
Conversion Agent is free with B&P
Ads Agent is $49/mo + 10%
questions.explain: Loyalty Agent is $49/mo including 500 SMS + 100 AI calls. B&P is free + 2.7%/txn; Conversion is $49/mo + 10% (needs B&P); Ads pricing is TBD.

questions.q: How does Zoca's subscription and billing model work?
options: A separate subscription per agent, each on its own cycle
One subscription on one billing cycle; adding agents joins the same subscription and renewals consolidate
Monthly only, with no annual option
A long-term contract with early-termination penalties
questions.explain: One subscription, one billing cycle — adding an agent joins the same subscription, renewals consolidate, and there are no long-term contracts.

questions.q: What is true about the setup fee?
options: There is no setup fee
There is a setup fee, waived only on the yearly (annual) plan — use it as a reason to go annual
The setup fee is always $290
The setup fee applies only to annual plans
questions.explain: There is a real setup fee, waived only on the yearly plan. Never say 'no setup fee' and never state the amount — frame the waiver as a reason to go annual.

questions.q: Which lead-prediction signal indicates a strong best-fit prospect?
options: At least 60 leads in 6 months
At least 100 leads per month
Any prospect in beauty regardless of leads
Pending Sales Ops review
questions.explain: The decided lead-prediction signal is at least 60 leads per 6 months — settled, not pending Sales Ops.
